title: Forest School
strapline: Weather, woods and freedom — learning with the whole self.
intent: Regular time in a natural space, in all weathers, builds a deep, first-hand connection with the living world and the seasons.
Open natural ground invites big, brave physical play — climbing, balancing, carrying, digging — that builds strength and confidence.
Assessing and taking safe risks — a log to balance on, a tree to climb — grows real resilience and self-belief.
Nature is the richest possible resource for curiosity, close looking and 'I wonder why' questions.
The freedom, space and calm of the outdoors especially helps children who find the indoors hard.
implementation: Go regularly and in all weathers, with the right clothing, so children experience the place changing through the seasons.
Follow the children's fascinations — a minibeast, a puddle, a fallen tree — rather than a fixed plan.
Support safe risk-taking: teach how to climb, carry sticks and use tools safely, then step back and trust them.
Wonder alongside them: 'I wonder why the leaves have changed colour', 'Where do you think that beetle is going?'
Bring in real skills — knots, fire (with ratios and rules), whittling, shelter-building — appropriate to age.
Notice and name the living world and the seasons, and care for the creatures and plants you find.
Keep it unhurried — the learning is in the freedom, the weather and the wondering, not in an activity.
key_questions: What has changed in our woods since we were last here?
I wonder why that is — what do you think?
How can you climb that safely — where will you put your feet?
What have you found — where do you think it lives?
How can we look after this place and its creatures?

impact.text: Children explore, care for and talk about the natural world and how it changes with the seasons.
Children climb, balance, carry and dig, building whole-body strength, coordination and confidence.
Children assess and take safe risks and keep going when things are hard, growing real resilience.
Children ask 'why' and 'how' questions about what they find and notice, and offer their own ideas.
Children handle creatures and plants gently and show care for the living world.
Children use rich talk to describe what they see, hear and wonder outdoors.

enhancements: All-weather clothing so the woods work in every season.
Ropes, tarps and pegs for shelter- and den-building.
Magnifiers, bug pots and collection bags for close looking.
Real tools for whittling, digging and, with the right ratios, fire.
A regular base and a fire circle or gathering spot the group returns to.
Seasonal projects — planting, harvesting, tracking a tree through the year.

playing_exploring: Children explore a rich, changing natural world with freedom and all their senses.
They take safe risks and find out what their bodies can do outdoors.
active_learning: Children persist with real challenges — a climb, a shelter, a cold day — and see them through.
creating_thinking: Children ask their own questions about the natural world and test out their ideas and theories.
